title: Paint the Fence Posts

concept.title: Two states: the last two posts have the same colour, or different colours
body: A fence has `n` posts in a row, and you have `k` colours. Every post gets one colour, but **no three posts in a row may have the same colour**. How many different paintings are there? For `n = 3` and `k = 2` the answer is 6 (all 8 paintings except the two single-colour ones). Print the answer modulo 1 000 000 007.

What do we need to know about the posts painted so far to continue? Only whether the **last two posts have the same colour** (then the next post must differ) or **different colours** (then the next post may copy the last one or differ). So keep two numbers: `same` is the number of paintings whose last two posts have the same colour, and `diff` is the number whose last two posts differ. The first post has `k` paintings and no pair yet, so we start with `same = 0`, `diff = k`.

body.code:
same, diff = 0, k                     # after the first post
for _ in range(n - 1):
    same, diff = diff, (same + diff) * (k - 1) % MOD
print((same + diff) % MOD)

body: Why these steps? A new post that **repeats** the last colour is possible only after a pair of different colours: new `same = diff`. A new post with a **new** colour has `k - 1` choices after any painting: new `diff = (same + diff) * (k - 1)`. The state has just two numbers, so this takes O(n) time and O(1) memory. Take the remainder before multiplying so the numbers fit in 64 bits.

statement: A fence has `n` posts in a row and there are `k` colours. Each post is painted with one colour, and no three consecutive posts may have the same colour. Print the number of different ways to paint the fence, modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: One line with two numbers `n` and `k`: the number of fence posts and the number of colours.
outputFormat: Print one number: the number of ways modulo 1000000007.

examples.note: Of the 8 paintings with two colours only AAA and BBB are not allowed: 6.
With one colour three posts must have the same colour: 0.

hints: Remember only two numbers: paintings whose last two posts are equal, and paintings whose last two posts differ.
A post can repeat the colour only after two different ones; a post can change the colour in k - 1 ways after anything.
Start with same = 0 and diff = k after the first post.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())

# Your code here

explanation: Two counts are kept: paintings whose last two posts have the same colour and paintings whose last two posts differ. A post that repeats the colour is possible only after a pair of different colours, and a post with a new colour has k - 1 choices after any painting; the answer is the sum of the two counts.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())

MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
same, diff = 0, k % MOD
for _ in range(n - 1):
    same, diff = diff, (same + diff) % MOD * ((k - 1) % MOD) % MOD
print((same + diff) % MOD)
